title: A White Hare on Bare Ground

scenes.tts: In fall, a snowshoe hare's brown fur turns white over several weeks. On snow, the white hare is hard to see. But what if the snow melts early, and the hare is still white? What happens to this hare?
scenes.visual: Brown hare on brown ground turns white as ground becomes snow; hard to see; snow melts, white hare on bare ground, big question mark.

scenes.tts: An adaptation is an inherited trait. It helps a living thing survive and reproduce, which means have young. Inherited means the trait passes from parents to their young. A hare's white coat is one adaptation.
scenes.visual: Word chip adaptation, chain inherited trait to survive and have young; parent hare passes coat trait to young hares.
scenes.narration: An adaptation is an inherited trait. It helps a living thing survive and reproduce, which means have young. Inherited means the trait passes from parents to their young. A hare's white coat is one adaptation.

scenes.tts: A physical adaptation is a feature of the body. It can be a body covering, a color, or a structure. A heron's long legs are a structure. A behavioral adaptation is an action. Migration is a regular journey between places used in different seasons. Monarch butterflies fly south in fall.
scenes.visual: Two columns: physical (hare coat, heron legs grow) and behavioral (migration arrow, monarchs south in fall).
scenes.narration: A physical adaptation is a feature of the body. It can be a body covering, a color, or a structure. A heron's long legs are a structure. A behavioral adaptation is an action. Migration is a regular journey between places used in different seasons. Monarch butterflies fly south in fall.

scenes.tts: The hare's white coat is camouflage. Camouflage is coloring that helps an animal blend in with its background. On snow, the white coat helps hide the hare. It does not make the hare invisible. On bare brown ground, the same coat stands out. That is a trade-off. A trade-off means a trait helps in one way but costs in another.
scenes.visual: Two panels, white hare on snow (blends in) and on bare ground (stands out), predator looks at each; helps and costs chips pulse.
scenes.narration: The hare's white coat is camouflage. Camouflage is coloring that helps an animal blend in with its background. On snow, the white coat helps hide the hare. It does not make the hare invisible. On bare brown ground, the same coat stands out. That is a trade-off. A trade-off means a trait helps in one way but costs in another.

scenes.tts: Hares in one forest are not all alike. In Montana, some hares turned white earlier than others. These differences between individuals are called variation. A single hare cannot decide to change color. Change happens to a population, all the members of one species in one area. Hares whose inherited timing fits the snow may survive and have more young. Over many generations, that timing can become more common.

scenes.tts: So what happens to a white hare when the snow melts early? It stands out on bare brown ground. Predators can spot it more easily. A single hare cannot choose a new coat. Only populations change, over many generations.
